property_summary: After any call to updateWinnersPerPeriod, winnersPerPeriod must be updated to the provided amount if the call succeeds, but the buggy require(false) causes every call to revert, so winnersPerPeriod can never be changed from its initial value.

After any successful call to updateWinnersPerPeriod, winnersPerPeriod equals the passed argument; the bug always reverts, so winnersPerPeriod can never equal any value other than its initial 2 after a call.
After any call to updateWinnersPerPeriod with an admin caller, winnersPerPeriod must be updatable; the buggy require(false) prevents any admin from ever changing it from its initial value of 2.

After any call to updateWinnersPerPeriod from an admin caller, the call either reverts (for the buggy version) or succeeds and updates winnersPerPeriod (for the correct version), which means the only way winnersPerPeriod can remain at its initial value of 2 after an admin call is if the call reverted; since the bug always reverts, a successful call (no revert) must set winnersPerPeriod to the passed amount, and this difference is observable through a revert boolean.

After any admin caller calls updateWinnersPerPeriod with a valid new amount, if the call does not revert and winnersPerPeriod is subsequently queried, it must equal the passed new amount; the bug makes every call revert, so winnersPerPeriod can never change from its initial value.
After any external call to updateWinnersPerPeriod, the winnersPerPeriod variable should only change when the sender has admin access; in the buggy version, anyone can change it.
For any caller that is not an admin, calling updateWinnersPerPeriod must not change the value of winnersPerPeriod; the mutant breaks this by allowing a non-admin to modify it.
After any call to updateWinnersPerPeriod by a non-admin, winnersPerPeriod must remain unchanged; the mutant allows any caller to modify it.
After any external call to updateWinnersPerPeriod, the value of winnersPerPeriod must revert if the caller is not an admin; the buggy version allows any caller to succeed.
For any caller that is not an admin, a call to updateWinnersPerPeriod must revert; the mutant allows it to succeed, thereby changing winnersPerPeriod.
For any admin caller, updateWinnersPerPeriod should set winnersPerPeriod to the passed value, but the mutant always reverts, leaving winnersPerPeriod unchanged.

For any admin caller, updateWinnersPerPeriod should set winnersPerPeriod to newWinnersPerPeriodAmount, but the mutant always reverts due to the `&& false` condition, leaving winnersPerPeriod unchanged.

For any admin caller and any newWinnersPerPeriodAmount, updateWinnersPerPeriod should set winnersPerPeriod to the new value, but the mutant always reverts due to the && false condition, leaving winnersPerPeriod unchanged.
For any admin caller and any new amount, updateWinnersPerPeriod should set winnersPerPeriod to the passed amount, but the mutant always reverts due to `&& false`, leaving the old value unchanged.

For any caller who is an admin, a call to updateWinnersPerPeriod with a new amount will successfully update winnersPerPeriod to that new amount; the mutant always reverts due to the `&& false` condition, leaving winnersPerPeriod unchanged.
The `winnersPerPeriod` state variable after an admin calls `updateWinnersPerPeriod` with any amount should equal that amount, but the buggy version always leaves it as 2.

After any sequence of admin-granted calls to updateWinnersPerPeriod, the value of winnersPerPeriod must be set to the new amount supplied by the admin, but the buggy version always sets it to 2 regardless of input.
For any admin-granted call to updateWinnersPerPeriod(N), the resulting winnersPerPeriod() must equal N, but the mutant always sets it to 2 breaking the rule for N != 2.
After an admin calls updateWinnersPerPeriod with any value, the public getter winnersPerPeriod() must return that value, but the buggy version always returns 2.
For any admin-granted call to updateWinnersPerPeriod(N), the new value of winnersPerPeriod() must equal N, but the mutant ignores N and sets it to 2, violating this for N ≠ 2.

After a non-empty pickWinner call, roundId must be strictly greater than before the call; the bug keeps it unchanged, so a subsequent pickWinner with the same id would be allowed but will not be selectable again because isSelectionComplete[roundId] is already true, leading to a revert.

After pickWinner is called with a valid winners array, the stored `roundId` must be strictly greater than the value it had before the call; the mutant fails to increment it, so the invariant `roundId > previousRoundId` is violated for any such call.
After pickWinner(...) is called, the new roundId must differ from the roundId before the call; the bug fails to increment it, so a second call to pickWinner(...) does not revert.

After pickWinner is called with a non-empty winners array, roundId must strictly increase; the mutant fails to increment it, so a subsequent call to pickWinner again with the SAME roundId will revert because isSelectionComplete[roundId] is already true, breaking the property that the second call succeeds.

After pickWinner is called, the value of isSelectionComplete[roundId] must be true for exactly one roundId value; the bug fails to increment roundId, so a subsequent pickWinner call with the same roundId will not revert and will overwrite the previous winners, violating the invariant that each round is selected at most once.

After pickWinner is called, roundId increments by exactly 1, ensuring no gaps are created in the sequence of rounds. The mutant increments roundId by 2, creating an unreachable round index that will never have winners selected, breaking the linear progression.

After pickWinner is called, for the newly completed round (roundId before the call), isSelectionComplete must be true; the mutant skips the next roundId, so after two pickWinner calls, the skipped roundId has isSelectionComplete stuck at false.

After pickWinner is called, the next roundId value must be exactly the previous roundId plus 1; the mutant increments by 2, so the reference satisfies roundId == oldRoundId + 1 for every call while the buggy version fails for some input.

After any sequence of pickWinner calls, the final roundId is exactly the number of completed rounds (i.e., the number of times pickWinner was called), ensuring no gaps in round indices; the mutant increments by 2, causing roundId to exceed the count of completed rounds for any call.

The rule is that after each call to pickWinner, the roundId is increased by exactly 1, so the number of completed rounds (the count of roundIds for which isSelectionComplete is true) equals roundId. The mutant increments by 2, causing roundId to be strictly greater than the count of completed rounds after any successful pickWinner.

After any call to pickWinner(...), the round identified by roundId-1 must be marked complete (isSelectionComplete[roundId-1] == true), because the bug increments roundId before marking the current round, leaving the previous round incomplete.

After any sequence of pickWinner calls, the number of completed rounds (count of true in isSelectionComplete) must equal the current roundId because each call marks the round it operates on as complete before incrementing roundId; the bug increments roundId before marking, causing the count of completed rounds to be less than roundId after the first call.
After any number of calls to pickWinner, the round immediately after the last completed round (i.e., roundId) must be unselected, but the bug marks it prematurely as complete.

For any sequence of pickWinner calls, the number of completed rounds (i.e., count of true values in isSelectionComplete) must equal the current roundId, but in the buggy version the count is less than roundId because the wrong round is marked complete.

After any call to pickWinner(...), isSelectionComplete[roundId - 1] must be true because the reference marks the current roundId before incrementing, whereas the bug increments first and marks the new roundId, leaving the completed round unselected.
